text.deployment: The standard Sprint serves as a dedicated artillery spotter and battlefield reconnaissance asset. Its Beagle Active Probe and TAG system make it the preferred choice for units that need reliable forward spotting without offensive capability. Widely fielded from the Clan invasion era onward, the base Sprint is found in reconnaissance lances and indirect fire support batteries across Inner Sphere militaries. It pairs naturally with artillery batteries, Long Tom carriers, and any formation where precision indirect fire is a priority. By the Dark Age, production had expanded to multiple facilities, making the base Sprint one of the more accessible reconnaissance VTOLs for mercenary and independent operators.

Fielded from 3057, the C3 variant replaces the TAG system with a C3 slave computer, integrating the Sprint into networked lance formations. Rather than serving as a pure artillery spotter, the C3 Sprint acts as a sensor node extending targeting reach for C3 master-equipped fire support units. Ruchbah production was interrupted during the Jihad when Word of Blake forces occupied the facility, though the variant resumed production post-liberation. By the Dark Age, Lockheed/CBM Corporation on Furillo also produced the C3 Sprint, ensuring continued supply for formations operating in Lyran space.

Introduced in 3068 for ComStar and Word of Blake forces, the C3i variant strips all standard electronics to install an Improved C3 system. The design favors the C3i's decentralized peer-to-peer network architecture over the hierarchical C3 slave approach. Both ComStar and Word of Blake attempted to negotiate exclusive manufacturing rights without success. Word of Blake forces operated this variant from captured Ruchbah facilities during the Jihad. Post-Jihad production ceased as both original operators lost their status as major military powers, and the C3i Sprint became rare outside salvage markets.

Developed during the Jihad and fielded from 3076, the Interdictor variant replaces the Beagle Active Probe with a Guardian ECM suite. Coalition forces used this version to disrupt Word of Blake communication networks and targeting systems during the final campaigns of the Jihad. Assembled as a field refit from available Sprint airframes rather than produced on a factory line, the Interdictor saw continued use well into the Dark Age wherever rapid electronic warfare suppression was needed. Its availability as a universal field conversion means it can be found across many factions with access to Sprint stocks.

Introduced in 3056, the Laser variant trades the TAG system for a single medium laser, giving the Sprint a limited capacity for direct fire. This version appeals to commanders who want a fast platform that can threaten light targets rather than serve purely as a passive spotter. The loss of TAG reduces its artillery coordination effectiveness, but the added laser gives Sprint pilots at least some means of discouraging pursuit and engaging soft targets of opportunity. Found in units that value flexibility over pure reconnaissance specialization.

Introduced in 3056, the Troop Transport variant removes the entire reconnaissance electronics suite to accommodate a 2.5-ton infantry bay. This version sacrifices all of the qualities that made the standard Sprint effective and turns it into a pure emergency rapid deployment transport. Its extreme speed gives infantry units an insertion capability against time-sensitive objectives, though the light airframe offers minimal protection to passengers during a contested approach. Best suited for clandestine insertions or extractions rather than direct assault roles.

text.capabilities:
The SRM Carrier mounts ten forward-firing Holly SRM-6 launchers, though manufacturers other than Quikscell frequently substitute locally produced systems such as HoverTec launchers in the Federated Suns or NCK systems in the Draconis Combine. An InterComBust 180 internal combustion engine provides a maximum speed of fifty-four kilometers per hour, while a Communicator system and FireScan with IndirecTrack targeting handle battlefield coordination.

Four tons of ammunition allow sustained fire, though the vehicle's forward-fixed launchers require physical repositioning to change firing angles. Three tons of Simple Armor Plate Standard protection represent the carrier's most critical vulnerability. In direct combat, the SRM Carrier's life expectancy is measured in seconds. However, this fragility is considered acceptable given the vehicle's extraordinarily low production cost and the terrifying damage potential of a full sixty-missile barrage. A coordinated lance of SRM Carriers can strip the armor from a heavy BattleMech in a single engagement.
text.deployment: Every major military in the Inner Sphere fields SRM Carriers in significant numbers, typically in dedicated fire support lances positioned in ambush along expected enemy approach routes. The vehicle's devastating alpha strike and low cost make it ideal for defensive operations in close terrain such as cities, dense forests, and canyon systems where its limited range is less of a disadvantage.

text.capabilities:
The 3054 upgrade incorporated Lexington Ltd. High Grade ferro-fibrous armor, nearly doubling the vehicle's survivability. One Holly SRM-6 launcher was removed to make room for a Doering Electronics Glowworm Narc Missile Beacon. The Narc system was intended to mark targets for follow-on missile strikes with improved accuracy, but many crews complained about the need to close to beacon range before their advanced munitions could make any difference.

The InterComBust 180 engine and basic chassis remain unchanged from the standard model, preserving the carrier's familiar handling characteristics. Six rounds of Narc ammunition provide limited beacon deployment capacity. The remaining nine SRM-6 launchers retain the ability to accept multiple ammunition types for tactical flexibility.
text.deployment: The 3054 upgrade was distributed among Federated Commonwealth regimental combat teams, with Oliver serving as the primary production site. The Narc variant's unpopularity led to limited adoption, with most units preferring the subsequent C3 revision. Sales opened to the broader Inner Sphere after the fall of Oliver to the Free Worlds League during Operation Guerrero.

text.capabilities:
The C3 variant addressed the unpopularity of the Narc-equipped upgrade by replacing the beacon with a C3 slave unit and Guardian ECM Suite. Nine Holly SRM-6 launchers provide substantial close-range firepower, while the C3 slave enables networked targeting data from friendly units equipped with C3 master computers. The Guardian ECM suite disrupts enemy electronics and provides protection against missile guidance systems.

Lexington Ltd. High Grade ferro-fibrous armor provides significantly improved protection over the standard model, with eighty points of armor coverage compared to the base variant's forty-eight. The InterComBust 180 engine maintains standard mobility. This combination of electronic warfare capability, networked targeting, and improved survivability made the C3 variant considerably more popular than its Narc-equipped predecessor.
text.deployment: The C3 variant proved more popular than the Narc-equipped upgrade, with Quikscell producing it at Oliver and Richvale for distribution across the Federated Suns and Lyran Alliance. The combination of networked targeting and electronic warfare capability made it particularly effective in combined-arms formations.

text.capabilities:
The Word of Blake variant serves as a near-complete redesign. An extralight fusion engine replaced the internal combustion powerplant, boosting speed while freeing tonnage for substantially increased ferro-fibrous armor. The original Holly launchers were replaced with turret-mounted Streak SRM-4 systems, sacrificing raw missile volume for dramatically improved hit probability.

A C3i computer provides networked targeting without the vulnerabilities of standard C3, while Targeting Acquisition Gear designates targets for artillery and semi-guided munitions. A Guardian ECM suite rounds out the electronics package. The combination of Streak launchers, advanced electronics, and improved mobility transforms the SRM Carrier from a disposable ambush platform into a more sophisticated fire support vehicle.
text.deployment: The Word of Blake variant was produced by Aldis Industries on Terra during the Jihad era, with the extralight fusion engine suggesting dedicated factory production rather than field refit. Production ceased following the liberation of Terra. The Streak SRM variant saw action throughout the Blakist campaigns in the Word of Blake Protectorate.

text.capabilities:
The SRM Carrier C mounts its ten SRM-6 launchers in a partial-traverse turret, vastly expanding the vehicle's ability to engage targets from multiple angles without repositioning. An upgraded 240-rated internal combustion engine increases ground speed to approximately forty-three kilometers per hour, a marked improvement over the base variant's thirty-six.

Hardened armor provides robust protection particularly effective against the Elemental swarms common in Clan warfare. The launchers accept Clan-specification ammunition for increased per-missile damage. Like its LRM counterpart, the semi-modular turret allows quick weapon swaps and rapid field repairs, making the variant attractive to mercenary commands.
text.deployment: Joint Equipment Systems developed the SRM Carrier C for the Rasalhague Dominion, with additional production at Quikscell plants on Kalidasa and Pandora. Other Clans rapidly trialed for or copied the hardened armor innovation, and mercenary commands have embraced the semi-modular turret design for its field maintenance advantages.

The standard Striker fills a fire support role in AFFS armored regiments, typically deployed in sections of three to four vehicles to mass LRM fire against concentrations of enemy armor and infantry. Planetary militia forces across the Federated Suns operate the type in substantial numbers, where its low operating cost and ease of maintenance suit resource-limited commands. The LAAF fielded the Striker in comparable roles during the FedCom era, and limited transfers to the DCMS placed small numbers in Combine garrison formations along the Federated Suns border.

The 3053 Upgrade entered production at Johnsondale following the Clan Invasion, distributing the Artemis IV-slaved LRM-15 and Streak SRM-2 configuration to front-line AFFS formations in the Draconis March. The upgrade replaced original models in priority units, with older variants cascading to militia forces. Lyran Alliance procurement accepted the 3053 Upgrade in limited numbers during the FedCom period, and a small batch was delivered to DCMS garrison units under the continuing sales arrangement.

The 3061 Upgrade adds a Guardian ECM suite, C3 slave link, and ER medium laser while retaining the upgraded missile battery. This configuration is assigned to combined-arms lances requiring enhanced electronic warfare capability and C3 network integration. The ER medium laser provides a fallback when missile ammunition runs low, making this variant a flexible and self-sufficient platform for extended operations.

A field refit adding an additional ton of ammunition to the standard missile battery, sacrificing secondary armament for extended operational endurance. Common among garrison formations expecting prolonged operations where resupply is unreliable. The Ammo variant trades close-range defensive capability for the ability to sustain high rates of fire, a trade-off that suits static defensive operations better than mobile offensive actions.

A field modification replacing the SRM launchers with a pair of ER medium lasers, eliminating ammunition dependence in the secondary weapon suite. Popular in areas where SRM ammunition is difficult to source, the Laser variant accepts reduced burst damage in the close-range role in exchange for sustained direct fire capability. Commands operating in logistics-constrained environments have adapted this configuration for extended patrol and interdiction duties.

An early field refit reconfiguring the weapon suite around a heavier LRM battery at the cost of the Streak launchers, optimizing the Striker for long-range bombardment over close defense. This configuration circulates among garrison and militia formations that prioritize indirect fire support. The (LRM) variant's long service history, extending from the Late Succession Wars through the present, reflects the durability of the basic modification and the continued utility of concentrated missile fire in combined-arms engagements.

A factory variant replacing the primary LRM battery with a Narc Missile Beacon launcher, intended to support combined-arms units equipped with Narc-compatible fire platforms. The Narc-equipped Striker provides target designation capability rather than direct firepower, and its utility depends entirely on the presence of accompanying assets capable of exploiting beacon locks. The configuration never achieved broad adoption, limiting its presence to specialist units conducting coordinated fire missions.

A production variant fielding a fuel cell engine, Guardian ECM, and dual MML-5 launchers in a sealed hull, designed for operations in contaminated environments including nuclear, biological, and chemical hazard zones. The sealed configuration accepts reduced firepower and speed in exchange for crew protection against environmental hazards. Issued primarily to formations assigned to contested industrial sites and former conflict zones where WMD contamination remains a threat.

An early field refit emphasizing close-range fire support by replacing the LRM battery with additional SRM launchers, suited to urban terrain and dense cover where long-range missile fire is impractical. The (SRM) variant circulates in garrison formations defending urban centers and fortified installations. Its long service history parallels the (LRM) configuration as a common modification applied to aging base-model Strikers through the Late Succession Wars and beyond.

The Stealth variant replaces the standard ferro-fibrous armor with electronically enhanced stealth armor, improving battlefield survivability through signature reduction. Issued primarily to MIIO-affiliated units and special operations formations, this Striker can approach adversary positions with reduced detection risk, enabling ambushes and flanking attacks unavailable to conventionally armored vehicles. Valiant's cooperation with Combine-developed stealth technology, facilitated through limited DCMS sales, contributed to the armor systems used in this configuration.

text.overview: The Strix Stealth VTOL is a landmark achievement in mixed-technology design, born from the ingenuity of Nova Cat refugees settled in Prefecture II of the Republic of the Sphere. Developed at Wayne Station on Shitara under the direction of Technician Pádraig, the Strix combines advanced Inner Sphere electronics and armor with Clan-grade weapons and targeting systems. The design emerged not from any official Republic military program but from the Nova Cat community's desire to contribute meaningfully to their adoptive nation while preserving their martial heritage. Four handcrafted prototypes were completed in 3117, and the Republic Armed Forces took notice quickly, licensing the design to StarCorps of Terra for full production beginning in 3121.
text.capabilities:
The Strix weighs thirty tons and carries a formidable combination of armament for its class. A chin turret mounting two ER Small Lasers provides flexible close-range firepower with a near-full arc of coverage, while an Ultra AC/2 in the front gives the vehicle reach that few aircraft of comparable size can match. A Targeting Computer sharpens both weapon systems, improving accuracy in even demanding tactical environments.

Protection relies on sixty-four points of Inner Sphere Stealth Armor, powered by the integrated Watchdog Counter-Electronics Warfare System. This pairing makes the Strix extremely difficult to acquire on sensors and suppresses enemy targeting locks, allowing it to approach defended positions that would deter conventional VTOLs. A VTOL Jet Booster extends its operational speed in burst maneuvers, giving pilots additional options for repositioning or disengagement.

The Strix carries significant trade-offs. Its Non-Standard Parts designation means replacement components are difficult to source outside the original manufacturing sites, making sustained operations logistically challenging. The mixed Clan and Inner Sphere technology base also demands specialized maintenance knowledge that most field technicians do not possess.
text.deployment: The Strix is assigned to light attack and reconnaissance forces within the Republic Armed Forces, capitalizing on its stealth armor and Watchdog CEWS suite to operate in contested airspace where conventional VTOLs cannot safely operate. The design pairs well with light ground vehicles and conventional infantry, providing air cover and suppressing enemy electronic systems at ranges that complement the capabilities of those formations. Initial deployment was limited to the four prototype units assigned to the Second Triarii Protectors in Prefecture II. Production variants from StarCorps were expected to distribute the design to a wider range of Republic formations, though the Non-Standard Parts designation initially constrained the number of units that could be kept in front-line service simultaneously.
text.battleHistory:
The Second Combine-Dominion War drove waves of Nova Cat civilians to seek asylum within the Republic of the Sphere, and the Republic's approach to these refugees proved unusually accommodating. Rather than forcing assimilation, authorities in Prefecture II allowed established Nova Cat enclaves a degree of cultural autonomy, provided subsidies to Nova Cat-owned businesses, and funded community programs staffed by volunteers from across the Second Triarii Protectors. Shitara, in Prefecture II, became the primary center of Nova Cat settlement, and its residents were actively encouraged to integrate by crediting aid work with citizenship service time.

Technician Pádraig had worked for years integrating Nova Cat technical expertise with Shitaran manufacturing infrastructure, aiming to combine the best technologies both the Clans and the Inner Sphere had to offer. His team operated without official Republic sponsorship, quietly sourcing components and adapting Clan systems to Inner Sphere production tolerances at Wayne Station. By 3117 they had handcrafted four Strix prototypes, demonstrating that Clan-grade equipment could be produced locally and integrated with Inner Sphere components without compromising battlefield effectiveness.

The results drew immediate attention. The four prototypes entered testing with the Second Triarii Protectors, who evaluated them in direct support of ground operations across Prefecture II. Their performance validated Pádraig's design philosophy, and the Republic Armed Forces moved quickly to formalize the program. StarCorps of Terra received a production license, and tooling at their Terra facility was underway with production scheduled to begin in 3121. StarCorps also initiated discussions with Pádraig's team about applying similar mixed-technology principles to a future assault OmniMech program for the RAF, extending the program's ambitions well beyond a single VTOL design.

text.deployment: The original SturmFeur remains in service across Lyran formations and successor state militaries. Produced at both Trellshire Heavy Industries on Sudeten and Defiance Industries on Hesperus II, the base model's proven ICE powerplant and straightforward construction ensure it continues to see widespread use in garrison and reserve formations. Its simplicity and reliability make it particularly valued where logistical support is limited.

The Assault variant entered full production at Defiance Industries on Hesperus II after Archon Trillian Steiner approved its manufacture following successful field tests. Combining a light fusion engine with an improved heavy Gauss rifle and Clan-grade missile launchers, it represents the most heavily armed SturmFeur configuration ever produced. Its mixed weapons loadout allows engagement across multiple range brackets, making it a versatile addition to modern Lyran heavy armor formations.

production.targeting: SturmFeur Highlight with BlindFire Radar and Artemis IV FCS

text.deployment: Released in 3149 from Defiance Industries on Hesperus II, the Cell variant was developed after study of salvaged Clan Hell's Horses vehicles. Its fuel cell powerplant reduces acquisition and operating costs while providing improved speed over the original model. Several Commonwealth regiments have received the Cell as a modern replacement for aging standard SturmFeur stocks, with its Clan-grade LRM launchers and Artemis fire control dramatically improving accuracy over earlier variants.

The Heavy Gauss variant is a radical departure from the SturmFeur's traditional fire support role, mounting a forward-facing heavy Gauss rifle that transforms the vehicle into a close-range assault platform. An Artemis-equipped LRM-10 and an extended-range medium laser provide supplementary firepower. The variant's effectiveness depends heavily on favorable terrain and tactical positioning, as its modest speed limits its ability to dictate engagement ranges.

Introduced in 3023 by Trellshire Heavy Industries on Sudeten, the SRM variant replaces the turret launcher with four SRM-4 racks and an additional machine gun. Designed as a close-defense escort for standard SturmFeurs, it protects fire support vehicles from enemies that manage to close within missile minimum range. Production occurred at Sudeten until the Clan Jade Falcon conquest in 3052.

The Steiner variant is a post-Jihad adaptation of the Word of Blake configuration, developed after Lyran forces recaptured Hesperus II. Defiance Industries retained the light fusion engine but replaced the B-Pods with heavy-duty M-Pods and swapped the improved C3 computer for an ECM suite. This configuration provides both missile firepower and electronic countermeasures capability, making it a valued asset in modern Lyran combined-arms formations.

Named in honor of the legendary SturmFeur commander Alan Gilmore, this specialized fire support variant carries an Arrow IV artillery launcher with mixed standard and homing munitions alongside five Thunderbolt 5 missile launchers. A TAG designator enables coordination with guided munitions fired by itself or friendly units. The Gilmore excels in the long-range bombardment role, embodying the indirect fire doctrine that its namesake pioneered during the Fourth Succession War.

The standard Stygian entered service with the Second Free Worlds Legionnaires in 3062 and spread progressively to other FWLM armor regiments and planetary militia formations. Primarily employed in the reconnaissance and light fire support roles, crews rely on the vehicle's high speed to avoid situations where its modest armor becomes a critical liability. The design operates most effectively when paired with heavier armored vehicles capable of anchoring a defensive line while the Stygian screens flanks and delivers missile fire from standoff range.
text.battleHistory:
The Stygian's origins trace to the early 3050s, when Captain-General Thomas Marik directed League manufacturers to bring modern weapons technology to conventional armor and militia formations at sustainable cost. BattleMech production consumed an increasing share of the FWLM budget, leaving planetary militia forces chronically underfunded, and the directive sought to redress the balance by developing capable armored vehicles using current weapons technology. Brooks Incorporated of Irian answered with the Harasser II, a substantially upgraded version of their proven Harasser fast missile boat. The Harasser II retained the hover platform and speed of its predecessor while incorporating a more capable missile system and extended-range laser armament.

Initial reception from the LCCC was lukewarm. Procurement officials questioned whether the Harasser II represented sufficient improvement over vehicles already in militia inventories to justify a new production commitment. Field testing resolved the debate. The Second Free Worlds Legionnaires put the Harasser II through exercises across varied terrain and conditions, finding it consistently superior to the alternatives. Force Commander Corrine Marik's personal endorsement broke the procurement deadlock. Brooks Incorporated renamed the production model the Stygian in honor of the Legionnaire unit, and production began at the Irian facility in 3062.

Early service with the Legionnaires generated feedback for an improved variant, and the Stygian Mudskipper entered production in 3065. This (Armor) variant traded engine output for additional protection and an expanded ammunition supply, addressing consistent crew complaints that the base model's armor was insufficient in closer terrain where standoff distance could not be maintained.

The Jihad brought significant disruption to Irian and the Brooks Incorporated facility. Word of Blake forces occupied the planet during the 3068 campaign, and a Blakist-modified variant appeared during this period, replacing the original weapons fit with pulse lasers, a lighter missile system, and an Improved C3 Computer suited to networked Blakist operations. Following the Jihad, the Irian facility passed to Republic of the Sphere oversight before cycling through subsequent ownership transitions. Production of the Stygian continued under each governing faction through the ilClan period, evidence of the soundness of the original Brooks design.

text.deployment: The Stygian Mudskipper variant, introduced in 3065 following field recommendations from the Legionnaires, offers improved survivability over the base model at the cost of top speed. The smaller Magna 145 engine limits flank speed to 129 km/h, reducing the variant's ability to disengage rapidly from close-range threats. The additional armor and expanded ammunition supply make the Mudskipper better suited to sustained fire support missions and operations in closer terrain. Militia commanders who prioritize endurance over sprint capability have favored it over the standard model.

It retains the hover platform's high speed and light armor of the original. Production was confined to the Jihad period, and surviving examples are rare.

The Stygian's origins trace to the early 3050s, when Captain-General Thomas Marik directed League manufacturers to bring modern weapons technology to conventional armor and militia formations at sustainable cost. BattleMech production consumed an increasing share of the FWLM budget, leaving planetary militia forces chronically underfunded, and the directive sought to redress the balance by developing capable armored vehicles using current weapons technology. Brooks Incorporated of Irian answered with the Harasser II, a substantially upgraded version of their proven Harasser fast missile boat. The Harasser II retained the hover platform and speed of its predecessor while incorporating a more capable missile system and extended-range laser armament.

Initial reception from the LCCC was lukewarm. Procurement officials questioned whether the Harasser II represented sufficient improvement over vehicles already in militia inventories to justify a new production commitment. Field testing resolved the debate. The Second Free Worlds Legionnaires put the Harasser II through exercises across varied terrain and conditions, finding it consistently superior to the alternatives. Force Commander Corrine Marik's personal endorsement broke the procurement deadlock. Brooks Incorporated renamed the production model the Stygian in honor of the Legionnaire unit, and production began at the Irian facility in 3062.

Early service with the Legionnaires generated feedback for an improved variant, and the Stygian Mudskipper entered production in 3065. This (Armor) variant traded engine output for additional protection and an expanded ammunition supply, addressing consistent crew complaints that the base model's armor was insufficient in closer terrain where standoff distance could not be maintained.

The Jihad brought significant disruption to Irian and the Brooks Incorporated facility. Word of Blake forces occupied the planet during the 3068 campaign, and a Blakist-modified variant appeared during this period, replacing the original weapons fit with pulse lasers, a lighter missile system, and an Improved C3 Computer suited to networked Blakist operations. Following the Jihad, the Irian facility passed to Republic of the Sphere oversight before cycling through subsequent ownership transitions. Production of the Stygian continued under each governing faction through the ilClan period, a sign of the soundness of the original Brooks design.

text.deployment: The standard Svantovit was distributed to second-line and garrison formations across every Clan from 2870 onward. Clans Blood Spirit and Hell's Horses operated the greatest concentrations, fielding the vehicle in numbers that reflected their reliance on conventional forces and Elemental Points in garrison roles. Clans Star Adder and Jade Falcon operated minimal numbers, with Jade Falcon limiting use to training exercises. Inner Sphere forces gained access to the design through Clan occupation zones and salvage from the Clan Invasion onward, with Draconis Combine production eventually restarting on Irece and later at Hyner.

text.capabilities:
The 'Masada' replaces the standard fusion engine with an XL unit, pushing the vehicle's flanking speed to 183 kph while freeing weight for a significantly heavier weapons suite. The five-ton infantry compartment and three tons of Compound Alpha ferro-fibrous armor are retained from the standard Svantovit, preserving the variant's core Elemental transport function. The rear hatch deployment limitation and the associated halt-before-deployment operating procedure remain unchanged.

The turret armament is substantially upgraded. A single ATM-9 launcher fed by three tons of ammunition replaces the Streak SRM launchers, giving the 'Masada' multi-range engagement capability at the cost of the standard model's point-defense focus. A pair of anti-personnel Gauss rifles supplementing the ATM system provide effective suppression against infantry targets, though their effectiveness against armored opponents is limited. The combination makes the 'Masada' a more capable fire support vehicle than the standard Svantovit, but the lighter anti-infantry weapons and heavier reliance on the ATM system require skilled fire control to employ effectively. As with all ATM-equipped vehicles, ammunition selection determines the engagement envelope, and logistics support for multiple ATM munition types is an ongoing operational concern.
text.deployment: The 'Masada' entered service with Clan Hell's Horse and Clan Snow Leopard forces primarily operating in the Homeworlds during the Jihad era. Production at Csesztreg supplied Hell's Horse touman units, while the Niles facility provided vehicles to Snow Leopard forces during the same period. The variant's combination of improved speed and heavier weapons made it a preferred Elemental transport when available, though limited production meant distribution remained concentrated among Homeworld Clan forces rather than spreading broadly to Inner Sphere theaters.

The original Svantovit served Clan garrison and second-line formations through the Succession Wars period and into the early Clan Invasion era. With cargo capacity sufficient only for conventional infantry platoons, it was progressively replaced in most units by the 2870 redesign as Elemental transport became the design's primary mission. A number of Clans retained original-configuration vehicles in reserve and training roles through the Civil War period, valued for their heavier turret armament when infantry delivery was not the primary requirement.

text.overview:
The Swallow Attack WiGE is a medium Wing-in-Ground-Effect combat vehicle produced by Nashan Diversified at their Furillo manufacturing complex. Drawing on the design heritage of Nashan's earlier Sturmvogel maritime patrol WiGE, the Swallow was developed to fill a fast-strike and close-support role for Lyran armed forces, combining the terrain flexibility of a WiGE with a respectable offensive punch. The design entered service in 3092 in an initial export configuration, then received a significant weapons overhaul by 3095 to better align with Lyran tactical preferences.

Known by its Germanic nickname Schwalbe within Lyran space, the vehicle found broad export success across most of the Inner Sphere, serving with mercenary units and second-line formations wherever speed and amphibious capability were valued. Its critics dismissed it as little more than a faster Hetzer, but operators familiar with WiGE tactics found its blend of speed and firepower well-suited to fast-attack operations across a wide variety of terrain.
text.capabilities:
The Swallow's performance centers on its 200-rated extralight fusion engine, which drives the craft to a maximum speed of 118 km/h. That speed is the vehicle's primary defensive asset, allowing crews to execute rapid attack runs and withdraw before heavier opponents can respond effectively. A flotation hull allows the Swallow to land on and operate from open water, extending its tactical reach to coastal, riverine, and island-chain environments that shut out conventional tracked or wheeled designs.

The main weapon is a heavy autocannon capable of firing both standard slugs and cluster munitions, offering flexibility against armored vehicles, infantry, and light aircraft. A pair of extended-range medium lasers provide reliable secondary firepower at moderate distances without any ammunition dependency. Together the weapons give the crew options across most engagement ranges the vehicle is likely to encounter.

Seven and a half tons of heavy ferro-fibrous armor protects the Swallow adequately for its weight class, though the coverage is concentrated at the front and falls off sharply toward the flanks and rear. The extralight engine is a significant liability under penetrating fire to the sides or rear. Against aerospace threats or naval gunfire the Swallow has no dedicated countermeasures, making fighter cover and coordinated mutual support essential in any environment where air or sea threats are present.
text.deployment:
Introduced in 3135, the Spotter variant was developed to meet demand for mobile forward observers capable of operating across the same difficult terrain as the rest of the Swallow family. Carrying additional sensors and fire coordination equipment, the Spotter advances ahead of heavier formations to identify and designate targets for artillery and fire support assets, then withdraws at WiGE speed before opposing forces can bring direct fire to bear.

The variant proved well-suited to worlds with broken coastal and island terrain, where its amphibious capability allowed it to reach observation positions inaccessible to wheeled or tracked alternatives. Lyran militia formations and combined-arms units operating in the early Dark Age found the Spotter effective at coordinating indirect fire against opponents attempting to exploit water obstacles as defensive barriers.
text.battleHistory:
Development of the Swallow began as Nashan Diversified's engineers sought to build on the commercial success of the Fensalir, a WiGE design produced in partnership with Johnston Industries. Evaluations concluded that the Fensalir's top speed was insufficient for the close-assault role Nashan had in mind, prompting the team to revisit the Sturmvogel maritime patrol WiGE as a structural foundation. The Sturmvogel's proven flotation hull and aerodynamic profile provided a workable starting point for scaling up to a heavier combat configuration.

The 3092 prototype carried a rotary autocannon and a snub-nose PPC, a pairing that underwhelmed LCAF evaluators. Lyran unit doctrine favored heavier-hitting autocannon systems over sustained fire rate, and the original weapons were considered a poor match for the supply chains and tactical culture of the Lyran armed forces. Nashan redesigned the armament package, substituting heavier and more range-capable weapons that aligned with existing Lyran logistics. The redesigned variant entered service in 3095 and quickly achieved the market traction the original had lacked. The original configuration continued in limited production as an export model, retained for buyers who preferred its higher sustained fire output.

The Swallow was adopted broadly by Lyran second-line and planetary militia formations throughout the Dark Age. The Twenty-third Arcturan Guards RCT on Furillo became one of its most prolific operators, exploiting the vehicle's water-capable hull across the island-dotted Eidsfoss sea to support the amphibious supply operations the regiment maintained there. In 3144, Grenadier units equipped with Swallows played a supporting role during a Kestrel Grenadiers operation against First Liao Hussar raiders in the Capellan March, using the vehicles' speed and terrain flexibility to track and pin the raiders across multiple systems before cornering them on Amiga.

text.overview: The Swift Guardian is the lightest and fastest element of Ulsop Robotics' Main Guardian Defense System, introduced in 2732 as the reconnaissance and screening component of the Guardian drone network. Built on a hover chassis at just five tons, the Swift Guardian uses its exceptional speed to extend the network's sensor coverage, harass approaching forces, and channel threats toward the heavier Main Guardian and Giant Guardian units waiting in prepared positions. Though lightly armed and armored, its role is not to engage threats head-on but to complicate enemy movement and targeting while the system's central computer coordinates a response. As an autonomous unit, it requires no crew and is produced to operate in large numbers. Its small size and high mobility made Swift Guardians difficult to suppress and effective at screening the approaches to defended installations, a quality that proved lethal to unprepared forces encountering the Muphrid facility centuries after Ulsop Robotics' fall.
text.battleHistory:
The Main Guardian Defense System originated with Ulsop Robotics, a firm that had built its reputation developing smart automation for the Terran Hegemony's Space Defense Systems infrastructure. By 2732, CEO Jay Frick proposed a new commercial venture: modular drone tank networks sold to planetary governments that lacked access to full SDS coverage. The concept drew on Ulsop's prior work but scaled it down to conventional ground defense, pairing fast hover scouts with heavier wheeled combat units and coordinating them under centralized computer control. The SLDF purchased the first production run but relegated the Guardians to base security duty following a serious incident at the Yakima Proving Grounds, whose details were never fully disclosed. Despite the setback, Ulsop pressed forward, maintaining production and research facilities on Zebebelgenubi, Murchison, and a dedicated skunk works on Muphrid's MacArthur continent.

The Amaris Coup proved catastrophic for both Ulsop Robotics and the Guardian program. Amaris' forces seized Guardian control centers across the Hegemony and turned the drone networks against the civilian population. When the SLDF fought its way back toward Terra, it destroyed waves of Guardians that the usurper's commanders had deployed as defensive screens. The few control computers that survived the fighting did not outlast the Succession Wars without Ulsop technicians to maintain them. Ulsop's facilities on Zebebelgenubi and Murchison were sacked and destroyed. A hidden remnant of the company clung to the Muphrid facility, which became the subject of lostech rumors throughout the Succession Wars. Those who entered the MacArthur jungles searching for the facility rarely returned.

When Clan Wolf arrived to incorporate Muphrid into the Star League Protectorate, they discovered why. The Muphrid research compound had never stopped running. Under Star League-era computer control, the automated factory had continued producing and deploying Guardians for centuries, interpreting every approach to its perimeter as a live proving ground exercise. On 27 June 3152, scouts of the Thirty-Seventh Wolf Striker Cluster made contact with what they assumed was a Capellan garrison, only to be met by swarms of Guardian drones in all three configurations. No matter how many the Cluster destroyed, more emerged from concealment, threatening to overwhelm the Clan warriors. The engagement ended only when the Thirty-Seventh's Elementals breached the compound and physically deactivated the Ulsop Autonomous Tactical Analysis Computer guiding the robotic tank swarm.

text.deployment: Assigned to reconnaissance and forward observer duties in Capellan Confederation Armed Forces combined-arms formations, the Swift Wind operates ahead of main armored and infantry columns to locate enemy positions and call in fire support from artillery and aerospace assets. Small numbers were issued to mercenary units serving the Confederation under long-term contracts. The design found particular application in anti-piracy operations along the Confederation's outer borders, where its planetary-scale communication capability allowed scouts to coordinate responses without revealing a main force's position.

text.capabilities:
The Swift Wind's mobility comes from six independently powered, Tablar-lined radial wheels with independent suspension and high ground clearance. A GM 60 fusion engine pushes the car to a top speed of 162 kph, fast enough to outrun most tracked and wheeled opponents. A scaled-down neurohelmet allows the driver to use their sense of balance for high-speed corrections while also providing wide-angle vision and infrared capability. One and a half tons of StarSlab/1 armor absorbs moderate fire long enough to disengage, but the Swift Wind cannot survive sustained contact. It carries no weapons.

The real payload is the CeresCom Recon Model 12k, two full tons of communications equipment capable of satellite uplink and direct transmission to JumpShips at standard jump points. A Swift Wind can scout any point on a planet without the enemy locating the parent force, and it serves as a forward observer for artillery and aerospace assets from far beyond direct-fire range. The system intercepts and triangulates enemy transmissions, compiling combined data into a three-dimensional holomap on the dashboard. A handheld remote unit allows the scout to operate up to 1,200 meters away while retaining comms capability at line-of-sight. Any direct engagement is a failure of mission planning. Speed and concealment are its only defenses, and a commander who deploys a Swift Wind in the main battle line has misunderstood the design entirely.
text.deployment: The ICE-Cargo variant strips out the communications suite entirely to free space for three tons of cargo and adopts a smaller engine that limits top speed to 120 kph. Without its reconnaissance equipment, this version serves as a light transport and courier vehicle for rear-area formations rather than as a true scout. Its distribution extends somewhat beyond typical Swift Wind markets, as the absence of sophisticated communications equipment simplified export licensing and made it attractive to buyers outside the Confederation who had no need for the base model's intelligence-gathering capabilities.

The ICE-Speed variant sacrifices nearly all protection and its entire communications suite to push top speed to 171 kph. Reduced to a half-ton of armor and stripped of reconnaissance gear, this version was used almost exclusively as a courier and liaison vehicle in situations where outrunning a threat was the only viable survival strategy. Its limited tactical value compared to the base model meant production figures remained modest, and most examples served in roles where raw speed mattered more than any capability a heavier or better-equipped vehicle could provide.

text.deployment: The ICE variant was introduced as a lower-cost alternative for Confederation formations and allied buyers operating on limited budgets. While it trades the operational economy of the fusion engine for a cheaper ICE powerplant and loses the cargo bay to accommodate the heavier engine, it retains the same top speed and full CeresCom Recon Model 12k communications capability. Production of this variant allowed the CCAF to field the Swift Wind in larger numbers across garrison and militia formations where the cost difference justified the trade-offs.

The standard Tamerlane Strike Sled equips fast-attack and reconnaissance companies within both the MAF and CCAF. Its combination of extended-range laser capability and short-range SRM punch makes it flexible across a range of engagement types, and its low logistics footprint allows deployment with formations that lack dedicated vehicle support elements. MAF standing units with priority access to Diverse Optics equipment receive the full-specification variant directly from the Krimari and Palladix plants.

Configured for sustained contact and anti-infantry operations, the Tamerlane Flamer variant mounts two medium lasers in the turret and a flamer in the front hull, eliminating dependence on ammunition entirely for extended sorties. The bubble cockpit receives a dark optical coating to protect the crew from the flamer's output at close range, which is sufficient to cause temporary blindness without the treatment. Used primarily for anti-infantry sweeps and long-duration patrol assignments where resupply is unavailable, the Flamer variant enters service primarily through official MAF procurement channels and sees more limited distribution in CCAF and mercenary formations.

The rocket launcher variant replaces the Marklin Mini SRM 2-pack with four one-shot ten-pack rocket launchers, two mounted forward and two to the rear, designed to maximize firepower output during a single slashing pass. The arrangement gives the Tamerlane RL a substantial burst of rockets across the engagement window before the vehicle withdraws at speed. The configuration is favored by crews specializing in fast-moving assault runs and shock raids, and it has developed a following among the more aggressive tactical schools in the MAF. The launcher housings partially obstruct peripheral cockpit visibility, a trade-off that crews accept in exchange for the variant's raw short-range firepower.

Introduced as a stopgap during the Diverse Optics supply shortage of 3073 to 3074, the Tamerlane 2 substitutes a standard medium laser for the extended-range model of the baseline variant. Though intended as an interim measure, the configuration found a lasting place in militia and export markets where simplified parts supply and reduced unit cost outweigh the shorter engagement range. CCAF units and Magistracy militia formations continue to field the 2 alongside the standard variant, treating the two as interchangeable for most patrol and screening assignments. Only the Detroit facility produces this configuration.

text.overview: The Tenmaku is the command element of the Teppō combined arms system, a purpose-built seventy-five ton trailer designed to protect senior DCMS commanders during engagements while maintaining complete battlefield awareness. Developed concurrently with the Teppō by Pesht Motors and assembled at the same Unity facility, the Tenmaku translates the Ryuken regiments' informal command-and-control doctrine into a dedicated platform. By physically separating commanding officers from direct fire while keeping them connected to a real-time tactical picture, the Tenmaku addresses the DCMS's identified strategic vulnerability: the preventable loss of experienced staff through unnecessary proximity to the front line. The trailer is towed by the Teppō and is not designed for independent operation.
text.capabilities:
The Tenmaku carries ten tons of dedicated communications equipment, including a full satellite uplink and real-time integration with a holographic mapping system, giving an embarked commander visibility of every combat unit across a planetary engagement. Two C³ Master Computers extend this coordination network to an entire company of units. An infantry compartment provides space for attached command staff. The trailer sustains its systems through a self-contained 10-rated fusion reactor, operating independently of the Teppō's fuel cell.

Though the Tenmaku lacks independent mobility, it carries a defensive suite including pulse lasers, machine guns, and an anti-missile system capable of engaging infantry threats and lighter vehicles. The trailer shares the same heavy ferro-fibrous armor profile, anti-missile coverage, ECM protection, and CASE-protected ammunition bays found on the Teppō, presenting a uniform defensive character across the combined system. This consistency allows crews of both vehicles to train and maintain their equipment against the same threat parameters.
text.deployment: The Tenmaku operates exclusively as part of the Teppō combined arms system and is not designed for independent deployment. It is towed into position by the Teppō and relies on the artillery vehicle for all strategic and tactical movement. The first Tenmaku units were assigned alongside the Teppō to the Ryuken-san. Broader distribution was planned to follow the same allocation model as the Teppō itself, with each assigned system including both the Tenmaku and Bokkusu trailers as standard equipment.
text.battleHistory:
The Tenmaku was developed as the command element of the Teppō system under the same DCMS contract that produced the artillery vehicle, reflecting the same institutional lesson: the Ryuken regiments' post-Jihad survival record showed that effective command required physical protection, not merely communication efficiency. Development emphasis centered on maintaining comprehensive battlefield awareness from a hardened position, producing a platform where the commanding officer could monitor an entire planetary engagement in real time without direct exposure to enemy fire.

The Tenmaku's design drew directly from analysis of DCMS command casualties during the Jihad, which identified that senior officers leading from BattleMechs or light command vehicles suffered disproportionate losses relative to their contribution to unit effectiveness. By embedding command capability within a heavily protected trailer towed by one of the most durable vehicles on the battlefield, the system offered a practical alternative. Initial deployment to the Ryuken-san was deliberate, placing the Tenmaku with the brigade whose doctrinal history had directly inspired its creation. Broader DCMS adoption was planned contingent on the Teppō system's overall field evaluation.

text.overview: The Teppō is a super-heavy wheeled artillery system developed by Pesht Motors for the Draconis Combine Mustered Soldiery, introduced in 3086 as the centerpiece of a combined arms package designed to modernize DCMS support doctrine. The system pairs the artillery vehicle with the Tenmaku command trailer and Bokkusu logistics trailer, forming an integrated platform that allows senior commanders to direct engagements from a protected position rather than from the front line. The design reflects lessons drawn from the Ryuken regiments' wartime survival record, which demonstrated that protecting command and logistics staff through combined arms coordination produced more durable formations than traditional doctrines demanding front-line leadership. Each Teppō is assembled by hand at Pesht Motors' Unity facility, requiring several months of construction per vehicle and limiting availability to small numbers of systems.
text.capabilities:
The Teppō rides a super-heavy wheeled chassis massing fifty tons more than a Behemoth, with ground mobility intentionally limited to short tactical repositioning. Strategic movement relies on DropShip or conventional aircraft transport. Its offensive power centers on an Ikazuchi Type 2 Sniper artillery piece mounted on a reinforced turret capable of rapid traverse across uneven terrain. Two Shigunga Arrow IV missile systems supplement the primary battery, typically loaded with homing and FASCAM munitions. When a supporting TAG-equipped unit designates a target, the Arrow IV launchers can concentrate strike power equivalent to an assault BattleMech's weapons suite against a target a full kilometer distant.

Twenty tons of New Samarkand Royal Heavy Ferro-Fibrous armor resist direct fire that would disable lighter vehicles. Three Yori Flyswatter anti-missile systems ring the hull, a Sipher Battlesys 11.6 ECM suite disrupts incoming targeting locks, and CASE-protected ammunition bays ensure crew survivability even if the vehicle sustains a catastrophic ammunition strike. Two Sperry Browning light miniguns provide suppressive fire against infantry. The Teppō's integrated towing system accommodates two specially-built seventy-five ton trailers simultaneously, connecting the artillery platform with the Bokkusu repair trailer and Tenmaku command trailer to form a self-sufficient combined arms system capable of sustained independent operations.
text.deployment: The Teppō's hand-built construction at Pesht Motors' Unity facility limits production to small numbers of vehicles, each requiring several months of assembly. The first completed systems were assigned to the Ryuken-san for field evaluation, with broader DCMS adoption planned contingent on operational results. The Combine intended to assign at least one Teppō system to each major combat formation if the evaluation proved favorable. Due to its extreme mass and limited independent ground mobility, the Teppō is transported to operational areas by DropShip or conventional aircraft, where it functions as a semi-static fire support and command platform. External interest from the Republic of the Armed Forces indicated potential distribution beyond Combine borders.
text.battleHistory:
The Teppō system emerged from an institutional reckoning within the DCMS conducted during the closing years of the Jihad. Fifteen years of sustained Clan warfare, followed by the calculated brutality of the Jihad, had inflicted losses on the Combine's officer corps that extended far beyond battlefield casualties. Experienced command and logistics staff proved especially difficult to replace, with their loss eroding unit cohesion in ways that surviving combat records made impossible to ignore.

Analysis of surviving units identified a consistent pattern. Regiments with robust command-and-control structures and willingness to integrate conventional forces alongside their BattleMech assets showed higher survival rates among their command and logistics staff than comparably engaged units following traditional doctrine. The Ryuken regiments embodied this pattern most clearly. Long dismissed within the DCMS for their Dragoon-influenced philosophy of combined arms coordination over BattleMech supremacy, the Ryuken endured the Jihad's worst sustained fighting with their institutional knowledge largely intact, even as their combat strength was ground toward ineffectiveness. The DCMS drew a practical conclusion: the Ryuken's approach was not a cultural eccentricity to be tolerated but a doctrine worth systematizing.

Pesht Motors received the development contract, tasked with producing a platform allowing senior commanders to direct large engagements from a protected position rather than from the line of fire. The resulting Teppō system translated the Ryuken's informal combined arms approach into purpose-built equipment. Initial deployment assigned the first completed vehicles to the Ryuken-san, whose institutional heritage had directly shaped the system's design philosophy. The Combine anticipated that successful field evaluation would prompt broader assignment across major combat formations, with the Republic of the Armed Forces monitoring the program closely and expressing interest in acquiring units or negotiating design rights.

text.overview: The Testudo Siege Tank takes its name from a Roman military formation, a tribute to the Marian Hegemony's enduring affection for classical Roman heritage. Designed and manufactured by the Alphard Trading Corporation on Alphard, the Testudo entered service in 3131 in response to growing unrest within the Hegemony's infantry ranks. The caesar of the time recognized that infantry morale demanded a visible, powerful support platform, and the Testudo was the answer to that demand. Built to fulfill a dual role, the design balances devastating long-range artillery capability with the ability to anchor a defensive line as a mobile support vehicle. The result is a vehicle that gives Marian infantry commanders both fire superiority at range and a solid armored presence when the fighting moves to close quarters, a combination rare among Periphery designs of comparable tonnage.
text.capabilities:
The Testudo's primary offensive tool is a turreted Marian Arms Lithobolos Arrow IV artillery system, giving the crew indirect fire capability well beyond conventional direct-fire ranges. Carrying three tons of Arrow IV ammunition, crews can select from a variety of warhead types to suit different tactical situations, from anti-armor salvos to anti-infantry munitions. The flexibility this provides makes the Testudo useful across a wide range of mission profiles, though it burns through ammunition rapidly during sustained fire missions.

For direct engagements, the Imperator Automatic Ultra AC/10 provides a hard-hitting main weapon capable of double-tap fire when the tactical situation allows. Two SperryBrowning Light Machine Guns, one turret-mounted and one fixed in the hull front, round out the armament and give the crew a reasonable answer to infantry threats at close range.

Protection comes from 12.5 tons of Lorica Progressia ferro-fibrous armor backed by CASE, which limits blast damage to the crew in the event of an ammunition cook-off. The Omni 225 fuel cell engine keeps the vehicle's heat signature manageable and reduces fire risk compared to fusion alternatives. The trade-off is a modest top speed that leaves the Testudo vulnerable to fast flanking attacks. The machine guns, while effective against unarmored infantry, offer little deterrence against battle armor or faster assault units pressing a close engagement.
text.deployment: The Testudo is deployed in dedicated fire support lances attached to Marian Hegemony Armed Forces infantry formations, typically operating two to four vehicles per company. Standard doctrine calls for the tanks to establish firing positions at the outer edge of indirect fire range before an assault, shifting forward as the infantry advances to maintain coverage. The Arrow IV system requires a relatively stable platform during bombardment, making terrain selection critical for the crew. In defensive operations, Testudos are often positioned in hull-down emplacements, using their heavy armor and artillery reach to deny ground rather than maneuver against the enemy. The design has seen limited export beyond the Hegemony and remains almost exclusively a Marian asset.
text.battleHistory:
The Marian Hegemony's infantry corps had long operated in the shadow of the Hegemony's BattleMech forces, receiving less funding and less prestige. By the early 3130s, discontent among infantry ranks had grown severe enough that Caesar Ignatius O'Reilly's government felt compelled to respond. Rather than simply adjusting pay or benefits, the administration chose a more visible solution: a new heavy tracked vehicle designed specifically to support and fight alongside infantry formations. The Alphard Trading Corporation, already in the middle of an ambitious industrial expansion following the Jihad, was commissioned to design and build what would become the Testudo.

The tank entered service in 3131 to a mixed reception. Marian infantry commanders complained about the accuracy of the artillery system during sustained fire and the speed at which it depleted ammunition under combat conditions. The Testudo's potential took time to emerge, requiring a generation of combined-arms operations before crews and commanders learned to integrate it effectively into their formations.

One engagement that shifted perceptions came during the fighting on Ibstock in 3136. An Oriente Protectorate infantry force, cornered in a fortified position at Portsmouth Gorge by a pursuing BattleMech lance, called for armored relief. The arriving Testudos exploited a critical moment of overconfidence: the lead Catapult pressed into the pass without respecting a thin Oriente picket line, and Arrow IV salvos from the approaching vehicles dismantled the lead elements of the lance before the survivors could withdraw. The infantry mopped up what remained. After-action reports from the engagement circulated widely through the MHAF and began to rehabilitate the Testudo's standing among skeptical commanders.

A separate incident reinforced the design's reputation for durability. A company of Testudos escorting a supply column on Marik was ambushed by Clan Wolf raiding forces. With no room to maneuver clear, the company commander gathered the convoy tightly and positioned the Testudos around it in a defensive ring. The vehicles absorbed repeated attacks from faster Clan units probing for weaknesses, holding long enough for headquarters to scramble aerospace assets that drove the raiders off. The Testudo emerged from the engagement with its reputation for toughness firmly established.

text.overview: Earthwerks-FWL, Incorporated introduced the Thang-Ta shortly before the Jihad as a straightforward, cost-effective infantry transport built for the Free Worlds League's combined-arms doctrine. Simple construction kept production costs low without sacrificing the durability required on contested worlds. When the Jihad shattered the League into warring splinter states, the Thang-Ta proved well suited to the chaotic conditions that followed. Affordable to manufacture and maintain, the vehicle became a staple carrier for the Regulan Fiefs and other successor states struggling to field viable ground forces across a prolonged period of political fragmentation. Its adaptability to varied theaters, from disputed border worlds to urban pacification roles, cemented its reputation as a reliable workhorse. When Captain-General Jessica Marik oversaw the reunification of the Free Worlds League, the Thang-Ta had already proven its value across decades of continuous service with multiple successor states.
text.capabilities:
The Thang-Ta carries an infantry squad into combat aboard a sturdy wheeled chassis powered by a Magna 70 fusion engine, reaching a top speed just over 150 kilometers per hour. That speed is the vehicle's most reliable asset and its primary defensive tool. Valiant Chainmail ferro-fibrous armor provides solid protection for a vehicle of this weight class, allowing the Thang-Ta to absorb fire while delivering its passengers to the objective.

The armament consists of two Magna Mk IV Extended-Range Small Lasers mounted in a turret, offering full-circle coverage without heat concerns. Against lightly armored infantry or unprotected targets, the lasers perform adequately. Against serious armored opposition, they offer little beyond nuisance value, and crews are expected to disengage rather than engage heavier threats.

The turret has long been a source of frustration. Balky mechanical linkages mean that even glancing hits can seize the mount entirely, leaving the crew with no offensive recourse beyond their road speed. Earthwerks sacrificed creature comforts throughout the design to minimize weight and cost, a compromise noticed on extended deployments. The Thang-Ta is not a fire support platform and was never intended to be. Its value lies in delivering infantry intact.
text.deployment: The Thang-Ta serves throughout the reformed Free Worlds League as a standard light infantry carrier, assigned to combined-arms formations at the battalion level and below. It operates frequently in platoon-strength groups alongside heavier armor or BattleMech support, particularly in garrison and security roles on contested League worlds. Cost-effective construction has enabled deployment in substantial numbers. The Regulan Fiefs and several former League splinter states distributed the type widely across their ground forces during the Dark Age, and captured or transferred examples serve in non-League militaries as well. Logistics officers favor the vehicle for its reliable fusion powerplant and simplified systems, which minimize maintenance demands across varied operational environments.
text.battleHistory:
Earthwerks-FWL, Incorporated developed the Thang-Ta at their Tiber facility in the years before the Jihad, fielding the vehicle just as Word of Blake operations began fracturing the Free Worlds League into competing factions. Production at Tiber continued even as political control of the facility shifted over the following decades, first passing to the Regulan Fiefs as the Dark Age reshaped former League territory. The Thang-Ta participated in nearly every major conflict among the League's splinter factions, serving as a cost-effective infantry carrier across contested border worlds and pacification operations where more sophisticated vehicles were unavailable.

During the Victoria War, Thang-Ta battalions operated with the First Andurien Rangers through the Betelgeuse campaign and the difficult withdrawal to Sigma Mare. House Imarra's combined-arms assault overwhelmed the Rangers, forcing a retreat to Sigma Mare where Thang-Ta crews conducted repeated sorties to recover scattered infantry from across the small continent of Tropinado. Operating under sustained fire from House Imarra BattleMechs and tanks, the APCs breached enemy lines repeatedly. The final breakthrough came at heavy cost when Imarra forces shifted focus entirely to the carriers. Speed and armor preserved most troopers, but a fighter ambush en route to the Rangers' JumpShips negated much of the effort. Only two platoons of the Thang-Ta battalion lifted off Sigma Mare.

On Loyalty in 3143, First Loyalty Defenders units equipped with Thang-Tas faced Mu Galaxy's Nineteenth Wolf Cavalry in a Trial of Possession for the Kallon Industries facility. Thang-Ta crews drove through the Cavalry's lines in a suicidal charge that disrupted the trial and forced the warriors into a melee, ultimately pushing the Cavalry into retreat. The disgrace of that loss led to two Stars of Clan warriors being consigned to the solahma. A follow-on Trial in 3144 proved more costly, with the Wolf Cavalry adapting to the Defenders' tactics and obliterating the Thang-Ta company. With the League's reunification under Captain-General Jessica Marik, the Tiber facility returned to direct Free Worlds League control, and the Thang-Ta remained a standard component of the reformed League's combined-arms inventory.

text.deployment: The Thor served with SLDF combined-arms formations as standard artillery support from 2680 onward, accompanying armored and BattleMech commands across all five army groups. The SLDF also supplied Thors to House militaries through military assistance programs, spreading the design across the Inner Sphere. By the time of the Amaris Coup, Thors were present in virtually every major military on both sides of the conflict, making them among the most widely deployed artillery vehicles of the Star League era.

This stripped-down variant emerged on the Pentagon Worlds in the centuries following the Exodus, where Star League components could no longer be maintained or replaced. Military commanders substituted available materials, replacing the Thumper and its fire control with an AC/10, a quad machine gun mount, and a pair of heavy rocket launchers, while an ICE powerplant replaced the fusion engine. The result was a generalist combat vehicle suited to garrison and raiding roles rather than dedicated artillery support, representing the practical adaptation of a sophisticated design to the severe industrial limitations of Pentagon Worlds forces before Operation Klondike.

The original Thumper appeared in the arsenals of virtually every major military and mercenary command in the Inner Sphere during its three centuries of production. Brooks sold without discrimination to authorized buyers across all factions, and the vehicle became a common sight in formations from the Great Houses to independent Periphery states. Free Worlds League forces maintain the highest concentrations, but surviving examples spread through export sales and battlefield recovery. Most examples encountered by the mid-Jihad era are extensively rebuilt, carrying field modifications applied by generations of unit technicians to compensate for worn-out or unavailable original components. This older configuration lacks the ER small lasers, ECM suite, and CASE unit found in the revitalized production variants, as well as the improved armor protection of the later models.

The Thumper Angel entered service in 3090 with Tamarind planetary militias as the first production examples rolled off the Irian line. Brooks did not limit sales to Tamarind, quickly soliciting clients across the Inner Sphere and making the Angel available through the same commercial channels as its other products. The fuel cell powerplant and integrated ECM suite proved attractive to commanders seeking artillery support with built-in electronic protection, willing to accept lighter secondary armament in exchange. The Irian facility maintained continuous production through the ownership transitions of the Dark Age and into the ilClan era, ensuring steady availability. The Angel is well suited to combined-arms formations that can supply adequate ammunition but want to minimize logistical dependence on fusion fuel.

The Thumper Maxwell never progressed beyond prototype production. The Maxwell Planetary Defense Consortium began building examples in 3080, but persistent difficulties meeting manufacturing targets, combined with the experimental status of several key components, prevented the program from reaching reliable output. The limited number of completed prototypes were distributed to Tamarind militia forces, where they provided operational feedback that directly informed the refinements incorporated into the Thumper Angel. Following Brooks Incorporated's legal settlement with MPDC, independent development of the Maxwell variant was discontinued in favor of the production-standard Angel. The Maxwell now exists primarily as a historical footnote and as evidence of the broader post-Jihad effort to develop indigenous military production capacity in the former Free Worlds League states.

The TAV-1 emerged from the revitalization of the Thumper production line during the Jihad, built at both the Andurien and Irian facilities of Brooks Incorporated. It represents the first production-standard upgrade package of the revitalized program, incorporating the improved electronics, revised secondary armament, and protection features that distinguished the modernized line from older stock. TAV-1 units equipped reformed Free Worlds League forces during the Jihad and entered the arsenals of buyers across the Inner Sphere as Brooks resumed sales. The Andurien line supplied primarily League-aligned customers during the Jihad, while the Irian facility serviced a broader customer base extending into Republic of the Sphere territory through the early Dark Age period before ownership transitions altered the supply relationships.

The TAV-2 entered service in 3075 as a further refinement of the revitalized Thumper program, produced alongside the TAV-1 at the Andurien and Irian facilities. Incorporating additional improvements over the TAV-1 upgrade package, it served in the latter stages of the Jihad and continued into the early Republic era. The Irian production line maintained TAV-2 output through successive ownership changes during the Dark Age period, making it available to Republic of the Sphere units as well as customers in what remained of the Free Worlds League. Deployment patterns mirror those of the TAV-1, with the TAV-2 typically replacing the earlier variant in formations as availability permitted rather than being assigned to distinct unit types.
