text.overview: The T-12 Tiger emerged from House Davion's search for a conventional armored platform capable of meeting the threats posed by the BattleMech revolution of the Age of War. While most successor powers poured resources into fusion-powered walkers, Veridian Dynamics on Torrence delivered a tracked medium tank that matched or exceeded contemporary designs at a fraction of the cost. Introduced in 2478, the Tiger quickly became the primary main battle tank of the Armed Forces of the Federated Suns and spread to dozens of other militaries across the Inner Sphere and Periphery over the following decades. Its influence on armored warfare doctrine during the Age of War and Reunification War period established the Tiger as one of the most widely produced and operated conventional vehicles of its era.
text.capabilities:
The Tiger's primary weapon is the Federated Autoloader/10-B medium autocannon, a heavy-caliber system capable of defeating the armor of most contemporary combat vehicles while maintaining a high rate of fire. Two tons of ammunition allow for sustained engagement, though most crews carry standard armor-piercing rounds given the single ton available for the SRM pack. The autocannon's proven design and low maintenance requirements contributed significantly to the Tiger's appeal for mass production.

Supplementing the main gun, a Grizzly-3 Minigun mounts coaxially, providing effective anti-infantry fire in close-quarters engagements. An Archer SRM-4 Pack adds medium-range punch against armored targets, while two Borman-A5C Heavy Machineguns protect the fore and aft quarters from infantry assault. This combined armament package gives the Tiger credible capability against all target types encountered in combined-arms operations.

The Tiger's principal weakness is its protection. The Quantum Heavy Plate covers barely ten percent of the vehicle's total mass, sufficient to absorb hits from its own autocannon on most facings but vulnerable to heavier weapons systems common among contemporary BattleMechs and larger vehicles. The Veridian 220 ICE delivers reliable performance at a top speed of 64 kph, adequate for most tactical roles but insufficient to disengage from faster opponents once contact is made.
text.deployment: The T-12 served as the primary main battle tank for the Armed Forces of the Federated Suns throughout the Age of War and Reunification War, deployed in armored regiments and combined-arms formations across Davion space. Its low production cost allowed widespread fielding in both garrison and line units. As licenses spread to Lyran, Capellan, Combine, and Free Worlds League facilities, Tiger variants entered service across much of the Inner Sphere and Periphery. Reserve and militia forces continued operating the design for generations after front-line units transitioned to newer equipment.
text.battleHistory:
Veridian Dynamics developed the Tiger in response to House Davion's directive to field a capable main battle tank that could be produced quickly and economically across multiple facilities. The Armed Forces of the Federated Suns adopted the T-12 before the close of the Age of War, relying on it as the backbone of their armored forces through the Reunification Wars. The design's simplicity and substantially lower cost compared to fusion-powered alternatives made it equally attractive to other powers, and production licenses spread rapidly during the late 25th century.

The political alliance between the Federated Suns and the Lyran Commonwealth brought the Tiger to Lyran production lines in the 2480s, with Veridian's facility on Tamar among the first to operate under that arrangement. By the early 26th century, virtually every industrialized power in the Inner Sphere was operating some version of the Tiger. Licensed production appeared in the Capellan Confederation, the Draconis Combine, and the Free Worlds League, while facilities in the Deep Periphery, including Bordello Military Goods on Antwerp, produced the design for Hanseatic League forces and continued doing so well into the ilClan era.

The Tiger was showing its age by the Reunification War. Heavier and better-protected designs had emerged across the Inner Sphere, and the AFFS phased the T-12 out of front-line service before the war concluded. Several powers briefly restarted production during the early Succession Wars to offset equipment losses, taking advantage of the design's mature manufacturing base. No major production lines remained active by the nadir of the Succession Wars, and the Tiger survived mainly in reserve formations, planetary militias, and the occasional mercenary unit.

During the Davion Civil War, Colonel John Gordon of the First Avalon Dragoons served as one of Alexander Davion's principal field commanders, directing actions across dozens of Capellan March and Crucis worlds from the cupola of a modified Tiger. Gordon's capture and subsequent execution on Jaipur marked one of the civil war's most costly losses for the Davionist cause.

text.deployment: The standard Tokugawa serves in general combat and urban assault roles across all Draconis Combine formations. Combined-arms lances pair it alongside BattleMechs, where its turret weapons provide direct fire support while its chassis-mounted lasers offer close defense without requiring the crew to break their primary fire solution. The vehicle performs particularly well in urban environments, where the wheeled drive train provides reliable mobility on prepared surfaces and the mixed weapon suite can address the diverse target types common in city fighting. Broad distribution across both garrison and frontline units, sustained by the Proserpina production line, has made this the most encountered Tokugawa variant in DCMS service.

This field conversion modifies the standard Tokugawa by removing one ton of autocannon ammunition to accommodate a C3 slave computer. Designed for integration into fire networks anchored by a C3 master-equipped BattleMech, the variant allows networked targeting data to improve accuracy across the entire lance. The conversion requires no depot-level work and can be completed by unit technicians in the field, making it practical for units already operating the standard model. It saw active use in DCMS operations against Clan Ghost Bear and in border actions against the Federated Suns, where coordinated lance fire proved effective against Clan and IS heavy armor alike.

Developed as a field modification, this variant replaces the LB 10-X Autocannon with a thirty-tube Medium Range Missile launcher carrying three tons of ammunition, and adds a Target Acquisition Gear designator for artillery coordination. The reconfiguration trades the standard model's ballistic flexibility for sustained missile volume and the ability to support indirect fire assets. The MRM variant proved most useful in offensive operations where Combine artillery was available to exploit the TAG designation, and it found adoption in units serving on the Federated Suns border where fire coordination with artillery was a standard tactical approach.

This post-Clan Invasion field upgrade swaps the SRM-6 and Artemis IV fire control for a Streak SRM-6 launcher and a Small Pulse Laser, at the cost of one ton each of autocannon and missile ammunition. The Streak system fires only on confirmed target lock, reducing wasted shots and improving per-salvo lethality compared to the standard launcher. The Small Pulse Laser provides supplemental close-in capability against light vehicles and infantry in the same turret arc. The upgrade was adopted by crews who found the standard model's missile accuracy insufficient in the fast-moving engagements common during and after the Clan Invasion.

The TKG-150 represents the Tokugawa in its most austere form, a product of the Succession Wars' steady erosion of advanced manufacturing capability. Replacing the later design's fusion plant with an internal combustion engine of equivalent rating sacrificed operational range and reduced performance in adverse conditions, but kept the vehicle producible in the Combine's diminished industrial base. A standard Autocannon/10 in place of the LB-X model and reduced ammunition stowage further simplified the logistics burden. A single Machine Gun replaced the chassis-mounted lasers of later versions, providing minimal anti-infantry coverage. The TKG-150 served in defensive garrison formations across the Combine through the mid-3000s, and units transferred to planetary militia as the modernized fusion-engine variants entered frontline service.

The TKG-151 is a long-range fire support variant of the TKG-150, replacing the single Autocannon/10 with a pair of Autocannon/2s fed by two tons of ammunition. The reconfiguration traded close-in hitting power for extended standoff range, positioning the TKG-151 as a suppression and harassment platform in open terrain engagements. In practice the design found most use in defensive lines, where it could engage approaching formations at range while heavier-armed vehicles held the close perimeter. The TKG-151 served Combine garrisons through the early Clan Invasion period before the modernized fusion-engine variants phased it out of active service.

The standard Trajan replaced the Palmoni's Improved C3 with a C3 slave computer and Guardian ECM suite, integrating the vehicle into Republic command networks. This version represents the primary production model and is the most widely fielded variant in RAF service. It retains the full weapon suite of the original design while offering improved electronic warfare capabilities that make it better suited to the combined-arms doctrine favored by Republic forces.

The ICE-powered Trajan is a cost-reduced variant originally produced for Word of Blake second-line troops such as the Protectorate Militia. Replacing the fusion engine with an internal combustion engine significantly lowered production and maintenance costs. To compensate for the power reduction, this variant drops one anti-missile system and the extended-range medium laser. The twin multi-missile launchers are replaced by a single LRM 10 rack and a Streak SRM 6, sacrificing weapon flexibility for simplicity. The ICE variant remained in Republic service as an economical alternative for garrison forces where the full fusion-powered model was not required.

text.overview: The JI-100 Transportable Field Repair Unit is a 70-ton tracked recovery and repair vehicle manufactured by Johnston Industries. Introduced in the first quarter of 3074, the JI-100 was designed as a larger, more capable successor to the company's JI-50 Jifty. Following the simple philosophy of bigger and better, the JI-100 resembles the Jifty only in its mission profile, utilizing a heavy tracked tank chassis rather than the civilian truck-like frame of its predecessor. With a combined cargo capacity that dwarfs other heavy BattleMech recovery vehicles, the JI-100 quickly established itself as the premier field repair platform in the Inner Sphere.
text.capabilities:
The JI-100 is powered by a General Motors fusion engine that propels the 70-ton vehicle at speeds up to 50 kilometers per hour. Three front-mounted lift hoists, each capable of handling heavy loads, provide the vehicle's primary recovery capability. This arrangement allows the JI-100 to approach salvage from the front and immediately begin lifting operations, a significant improvement over the Jifty's dual rear-facing hoists. The vehicle carries 33 tons of cargo in its internal bay, nearly double the Jifty's capacity, with space for spare parts, tools, and recovered components.

Defensive armament consists of a pair of front-mounted machine guns with a half-ton of ammunition, intended to discourage infantry hijacking attempts rather than engage combat vehicles. Protection comes from 2.5 tons of standard armor. Detractors noted that the armor, while higher quality than the Jifty's industrial-grade plating, is actually thinner overall. Johnston Industries maintains that the JI-100 should never approach an active battlefield, and its sturdy chassis provides the durability needed for hazardous salvage operations rather than combat survival. The vehicle carries a crew of five.
text.deployment: The JI-100 has no known variants as of the ilClan era. Its single configuration has proven versatile enough for the full range of field repair, recovery, and salvage missions without requiring the field modifications that spawned multiple Jifty variants during the Jihad. Military commands across the Federated Suns and the broader Inner Sphere have steadily upgraded from the JI-50 to the JI-100 where budgets allow.
text.battleHistory:
Johnston Industries developed the JI-100 as a direct competitive response to Blue Bull, Inc.'s Nifty knockoff of their JI-50 Jifty. Rather than continue pursuing patent litigation in courts paralyzed by the Jihad, Johnston's leadership redirected their superior research and development resources toward creating a vehicle that would render the imitator irrelevant. The strategy proved sound. When the JI-100 debuted in the first quarter of 3074, it was met with enthusiastic reception from military procurement offices across the Federated Suns.

The design philosophy was straightforward. The JI-100 would be everything the Jifty was, but scaled upward. Massing ten tons more than the JI-50 and adding a third lift hoist, the new vehicle offered dramatically increased cargo capacity and recovery capability. The shift from a civilian truck-like chassis to a heavy tracked tank frame gave the JI-100 the ruggedness to operate in rougher terrain and more demanding conditions than the Jifty could manage. Three front-mounted hoists allowed immediate access to salvage as it was approached, reversing the rear-access arrangement of the JI-50.

Military commands quickly embraced the JI-100, and the transition from JI-50 to JI-100 proceeded steadily through the post-Jihad rebuilding era. The years since introduction proved Johnston Industries' strategy successful. The JI-100 left no room on AFFS support rosters for Blue Bull's Nifty, effectively ending the knockoff's market viability through superior engineering rather than courtroom victories. By the Dark Age, the JI-100 had become the standard field repair vehicle for any formation that could secure one, its combined cargo and recovery capability unmatched by competing designs.

text.overview: The Tribune Mobile Tactical Command HQ is a light tracked command vehicle developed alongside the Praetorian as one of two field-command platforms for the Republic of the Sphere's combined-arms regiments. Where the Praetorian serves as the communication nexus for a regiment, the Tribune acts as a forward scout element that extends the command network into contested areas. Each Republic battalion deployed three Tribunes alongside a single Praetorian, creating a web of sensor data and communications relay points that covered the entire operational area. Produced by Cyclops Incorporated on Skye and Michaelson Heavy Industries on Ruchbah and Terra, the Tribune proved highly successful during the Capellan Crusades and subsequent conflicts.
text.capabilities:
The Tribune carries five tons of communications equipment integrated with a Garret T10-series I/3 Guardian communications system, sufficient to feed large quantities of data back to its accompanying Praetorian while maintaining independent coordination capability. A Garret T-10 Series V targeting tracking system provides fire control and sensor fusion. A Remote Sensor Dispenser allows teams of Tribunes to expand sensor coverage by deploying relay nodes at strategic positions.

Guardian ECM disrupts enemy electronics and advanced weapons, while a Bloodhound Active Probe detects hidden units, making the Tribune effective in the scout role alongside its command function. Designed for front-line service where damage is expected, the Tribune incorporates several survivability features. A 160-rated fusion engine provides enough speed to avoid potentially fatal engagements, and Durallex Special heavy ferro-fibrous armor protects against lighter weapons. A Magna Mk VI extended-range medium laser provides the only offensive weapon, sufficient for self-defense but not sustained combat. A laser anti-missile system offers point defense without requiring ammunition, and four Garret Tread A-Pods protect against infantry swarming attacks.
text.deployment: The Tribune operates as the forward tactical element in the Praetorian-Tribune command system, typically deployed in groups of three per battalion. Its combination of communications equipment, electronic warfare capability, and sensor systems makes it the most capable scout-command hybrid in the Republic arsenal. Following the Republic's dissolution, Tribunes continued in service with successor factions and export customers, though the vehicle's reliance on advanced components makes it more maintenance-intensive than the simpler Quaestor.
text.battleHistory:
The Tribune and Praetorian were conceived together during the early 3080s as the Republic's military leadership worked to standardize its diverse force structure. Early prototypes were tested during the Capellan fighting of 3081 through 3085, where the concept of paired strategic and tactical command vehicles proved its worth in coordinating mixed Clan and Inner Sphere formations. The final production models debuted in September 3091, with every RAF line battalion receiving a lance of one Praetorian and three Tribunes.

The Tribune's ability to operate forward of the main command post proved invaluable. Commanders who could track disparate units scattered across a planet gained significant tactical advantages over opponents relying on more conventional command arrangements. The decentralized command structure that Tribunes enabled demonstrated particular value during the New Syrtis campaign, where forces used the vehicles to maintain coordination while Capellan command structures remained heavily concentrated and vulnerable. As with the Praetorian, liberal export policies following the Capellan Crusades led to widespread proliferation. Users who operated either or both designs developed homegrown customizations, resulting in a surprising number of field variants for vehicles with such a short service history.

text.deployment: The base Tufana is best deployed as part of a fire support lance with at least one artillery-capable or semi-guided LRM unit in the formation. In Regulan service it commonly operates alongside Arrow IV-equipped platforms, providing TAG designation at close range while the heavier carrier engages from concealed positions. The combination works best in terrain that offers the Tufana cover between designation runs, allowing it to tag a target, withdraw, and relay positioning as the barrage arrives. Commanding officers assign Tufanas to units with strict fire discipline, as the vehicle's spotting value is wasted when crews become drawn into direct engagements. In Canopian service the Tufana fills a similar role alongside heavy multi-missile carriers, benefiting from the additional indirect fire options the MML platform provides.

The iNarc variant substitutes the standard Narc Missile Beacon for an improved Narc launcher, providing access to a wider range of warhead pod types including ECM and explosive payloads. The multi-missile launcher is removed, replaced by a pair of medium pulse lasers in the turret and an extended-range small laser in the nose. This configuration suits operators willing to trade indirect fire support for better self-defense and reduced ammunition dependency. The Capellan Confederation has purchased this variant in greater numbers than any other buyer, favoring its sustained-fire capability for extended operations away from supply lines. Tactically it serves the same spotting role as the base model, but crews retain more flexibility in close engagements and can continue to function after exhausting iNarc pods if circumstances require.

text.overview: Buhallin Military Products, a Dieron-based manufacturer renowned for wheeled combat vehicles, introduced the Turhan Urban Combat Vehicle in 2530 to fulfill a Terran Hegemony Armed Forces requirement for a dedicated urban assault platform. Designed to support infantry in the dense, ancient street grids of the Hegemony's oldest colonial cities, the Turhan scored over competing designs by incorporating an articulating joint at the chassis midpoint, a feature that earned the vehicle an enduring nickname among its crews but proved essential to navigating tight urban corridors. Its combination of sustained energy firepower and a purpose-built infantry transport compartment made it a natural fit for combined-arms operations. The Turhan served the Star League Defense Force for generations and remained in service long after its original manufacturer closed, a reflection of the soundness of its core design.
text.deployment: The production standard Turhan, which incorporated ferro-fibrous armor from 2583 onward, became the most widely distributed variant in the design family. SLDF formations across the Inner Sphere operated the type as their primary armored infantry transport, and surviving units passed into ComStar's hands following the Star League's dissolution. The design reached Draconis Combine forces through captured and traded ComStar surplus, and became the primary Combine variant once Pesht Motors resumed production on Unity in 3072. Units manufactured at the Unity facility serve throughout Combine territory, and the configuration remains the reference standard for the Turhan family.

An XL fusion engine offsets the weight of the C3 master computer and additional electronics, while the infantry compartment contracts to four tons to accommodate the new systems. One machine gun relocates to the hull front while its turret companion is replaced by an anti-missile system, giving the crew some protection against the missile threats that standard Turhans lack. The C3 computer connects the vehicle to broader lance- and company-level tactical networks, allowing it to serve as a command node for BattleMech and vehicle elements operating in the dense urban environments where the Turhan's design excels.

text.deployment: The Original variant entered service with Hegemony Armed Forces garrison and internal security formations in 2530, equipping units assigned to stability operations and policing duties across Hegemony worlds. Its standard armor configuration was well matched to the lower-intensity threats typical of Hegemony peacetime service. When Buhallin transitioned the production line to ferro-fibrous armor in 2583, manufacture of the original specification ended, though surviving vehicles continued serving alongside the updated production variant. Attrition and the demands of the Amaris conflict gradually eliminated the original-armor examples from frontline inventories over the following two centuries.

The standard Typhoon serves primarily in urban garrison and planetary assault roles within the Armed Forces of the Federated Suns. Introduced in 3057, it is most commonly assigned to combined arms formations alongside infantry and BattleMechs, where its heavy autocannon engages armored threats while its missile systems suppress infantry in building-to-building fighting. It is issued across a range of Regimental Combat Team formations and planetary militia units throughout the Federated Suns.

The LB-X variant, introduced in 3065, shifts the Typhoon toward a more flexible fire support role. Twin LB 10-X autocannons allow the crew to select between cluster munitions against softer targets and standard solid rounds against armored threats. A C3 slave unit replaces the Beagle Active Probe, enabling the vehicle to share targeting data across a networked lance or company and improving the accuracy of the entire formation. Two Streak SRM-4 launchers replace the four Streak SRM-2 systems of the base model. This variant is most effective when integrated into a C3-equipped combined arms force.

The RAC variant, introduced in 3064, replaces the standard Typhoon's autocannon and SRM rack with a pair of Rotary AC/5 systems, dramatically increasing the vehicle's sustained rate of fire against lighter targets and infantry concentrations. ER Medium Lasers take the place of the standard pulse lasers, extending effective range slightly. This variant is well suited to anti-infantry and light vehicle engagements where high volume fire matters more than single-shot hitting power, and it is found in formations expecting to face enemy infantry and conventional vehicle forces rather than heavy BattleMechs.

The tracked Typhoon prototype was developed concurrently with the standard wheeled design as an alternative chassis concept. Though the tracked variant matched the wheeled model in both firepower and armor protection, the AFFS directed Jalastar to pursue the less expensive wheeled configuration for full production. Only a small number of tracked prototypes were delivered to AFFS test and evaluation units, and the variant never entered widespread service.

The majority of Tyrs serve with the Claws of the Ghost Galaxy and related Ghost Bear and Rasalhague Dominion combined-arms formations in their intended role as infantry transport and close support vehicles. Produced exclusively at Joint Equipment Systems on Alshain, distribution is concentrated among units with direct supply lines to that facility. Small numbers have been observed serving with planetary garrison commands and other conventional forces attached to Ghost Bear front-line clusters.

Produced as an export variant at Joint Equipment Systems on Alshain beginning in 3070, the Tyr (Kurita) was supplied to Draconis Combine conventional forces during the Jihad period. Its appearance in Combine service reflects the Ghost Bear Dominion's willingness to supply military hardware across what had historically been a hostile border, likely facilitated by the extraordinary pressures of the Word of Blake Jihad. Distribution within Combine forces was limited, and the type did not become a standard DCMS equipment item.

text.overview: The Vali Artillery Vehicle is a wheeled fire support platform developed by Veridian Dynamics during the Reunification War, designed to provide organic indirect fire capability at the regimental level within the Star League Defense Force. Adapted from the company's proven RR-4 recovery vehicle, the Vali integrated the Arrow IV missile system into an existing battlefield chassis, sharply shortening development time and allowing Veridian's engineers to focus entirely on weapons integration. Despite competing with more advanced designs, it proved to be the most popular offering in its class, and its ease of maintenance and spacious crew compartment earned it lasting favor among SLDF crews throughout the twenty-seventh century. Manufactured at Veridian Dynamics' facility on Ozawa, the Vali remained a familiar sight in SLDF artillery formations long after the Reunification War concluded.
text.capabilities:
Veridian based the Vali on its widely successful RR-4 recovery vehicle. This approach allowed engineers to focus entirely on integrating the Arrow IV launcher, which was mounted in a simple superstructure that also housed the crew and their ammunition supply. The result was a vehicle that SLDF crews appreciated for its reliability, ease of maintenance compared to tracked vehicles, and spacious crew compartment.

Though the Vali's wheeled chassis meant it could not traverse every terrain that BattleMechs or heavy armor could manage, it possessed more than enough speed and mobility to keep pace with the line of advance. Four tons of Horden ferro-fibrous armor protect against small arms and counter-battery fire, though the Vali is not suited to direct engagement with combat vehicles or BattleMechs.

Five tons of ammunition allow the Vali to sustain continuous fire for more than four straight minutes. Reloading is accomplished via large doors in the rear of the vehicle. A crew without access to additional equipment can load by hand using the Vali's own reloading hoist, though a dedicated support vehicle on the same chassis can cut reloading times by a third by lifting out empty missile magazines and dropping fresh ones in. The primary limitation is that same ammunition capacity, which demands resupply discipline and coordination with logistics to sustain operations beyond the initial engagement window.
text.deployment:
The SLDF's goal at the turn of the twenty-seventh century was to provide every one of its regiments a battery of Valis that could trail the front lines to provide close fire support. This would free the longer-ranged guns of divisional artillery battalions to concentrate fire on critical targets rather than routine suppression missions. Though the SLDF never fully met this goal, every regular army BattleMech and armor regiment could claim an organic battery of at least two artillery pieces prior to the Coup.

In practice, Vali batteries operated closely with their parent regiments, positioning behind the forward line and engaging targets of opportunity identified by forward observers. The vehicle's wheeled mobility allowed it to relocate quickly after firing to avoid counter-battery response, a tactic that SLDF artillery doctrine formalized during the later Star League period. Crews became adept at rapid displacement, often moving two to three times per engagement before the enemy could plot their firing position.
text.battleHistory:
The Vali's origins trace to a formal requirement issued by the SLDF High Command during the closing phases of the Reunification War. Seeking a standardized, affordable artillery vehicle that frontline regiments could field organically, the High Command solicited designs that could mount the Arrow IV missile system without requiring an entirely new development program. Several manufacturers responded with purpose-built proposals, but Veridian Dynamics took a different approach, mating the Arrow IV to their existing RR-4 recovery vehicle hull. The simpler design won out for practical reasons, entering limited service with SLDF units during the final Taurian Concordat campaign.

Veridian received a full-scale production contract in 2600, and the company's Ozawa facility ramped up output to meet SLDF demand. The Terran Hegemony held administrative control of the Ozawa plant during the height of Star League production, and the factory supplied batteries of Valis to hundreds of SLDF regiments during the era. The design's reputation for durability and low maintenance requirements kept it in production long after more sophisticated competitors appeared, and the Vali outlasted several rival designs that proved too complex or costly to sustain at scale.

The collapse of the Star League brought the Vali's fortunes into sharp decline. Ozawa, sitting on the contested border between the Federated Suns and Draconis Combine, changed hands violently in the early Succession Wars. The Federated Suns held the planet through the First Succession War and kept the Veridian factory in limited operation, but the Draconis Combine seized Ozawa during the Second Succession War and ended production entirely. Without a manufacturing base and with spare parts growing scarce, surviving Valis gradually disappeared from frontline service across the Inner Sphere. Scattered examples endured in the hands of mercenary commands, garrison forces, and minor Periphery states well into the late Succession Wars, valued as much for their simplicity as for their firepower, but the type never saw a production revival.

text.deployment: The base Vargr delivers infantry to contested positions under armor protection across Aurigan Coalition ground operations. Once troops are disembarked, the turret-mounted machine guns and medium lasers allow the vehicle to remain on the battlefield as a fire support platform rather than withdrawing. It serves Coalition forces throughout the Late Succession Wars era.

The LRM variant replaces the medium lasers with a single turret-mounted LRM-15 and eight rounds of ammunition, trading close-range laser capability for indirect fire support. This allows the vehicle to engage at longer ranges alongside its machine guns, and provides a fire support option when infantry is not embarked. Introduced in 2945, one year after the base model.

The standard transport configuration served as the backbone of SLDF airborne operations. It carried a full platoon of infantry in its central bay along with a forward pulse laser for suppressive fire and two wing-mounted medium lasers for strafing. Assigned on a three-to-one ratio against all specialist configurations combined, the transport accounted for the majority of Vector production and was found in every SLDF infantry brigade and airborne formation from mid-century onward.

The Attack configuration replaced the infantry transport capacity with a dedicated close air support weapons fit. A single nose-mounted medium laser and a pair of wing-mounted SRM 4 launchers replaced the troop bay payload, giving crews the ability to engage light armor and massed infantry from a standoff distance. Attack Vectors were present in every SLDF divisional air wing and operated in mixed formations alongside transport and scout variants to provide on-call fire support to ground elements.

The EW configuration converted the Vector into a dedicated electronic warfare platform by replacing the infantry bay with a Guardian ECM Suite. A Target Acquisition Gear unit was fitted on a dorsal mast, allowing the craft to support artillery and missile strikes by designating targets. The standard weapons suite was retained. EW Vectors were assigned to divisional signals and electronic warfare elements and operated closely alongside ground-based jamming and intercept units across all theaters of SLDF operations.

The Scout configuration installed a Beagle Active Probe in place of the infantry complement, optimizing the craft for forward reconnaissance and the detection of concealed enemy units. Like the EW variant, it added a mast-mounted Target Acquisition Gear unit to support indirect fire coordination. Scout Vectors were assigned to divisional reconnaissance formations and typically operated in paired patrols or small groups, often working alongside EW-configured aircraft to provide real-time battlefield intelligence to SLDF commanders.

text.deployment: The standard Vedette serves as the workhorse of vehicle formations across the Inner Sphere, deployed in cavalry and dragoon roles where its high top speed allows rapid response and repositioning. Its most effective doctrine emphasizes pack tactics: multiple Vedettes concentrating fire on a single target from different angles to overcome the individual firepower limitation. The design is a staple of convoy escort, flank security, and fast pursuit operations. It serves in virtually every House army and most mercenary armor battalions, and its presence in garrison and line formations is so common that military planners routinely assume its availability when designing combined arms operations. The standard variant remains in production across more factories and in greater numbers than any other configuration.

'Doris' Delight' is a unique one-off modification developed during the FedCom Civil War by then-Private Daley after his crew's original vehicle was destroyed and casualties ran high. Using a salvaged extra-light fusion engine from a destroyed BattleMech and reworked internals, Daley produced a significantly faster vehicle carrying a Gauss rifle and nearly ten tons of armor. The vehicle served through multiple engagements until its destruction on New Avalon during the opening months of the Jihad. This variant cannot be replicated from the modification alone, as it required specific salvage components and improvised engineering. It is documented for record purposes as a combat record curiosity rather than a producible configuration.

The AC/10 variant is a Free Worlds League refit that replaced the Vedette's standard ICE with a salvaged Magna fusion engine, freeing sufficient weight to install an AC/10 and making the vehicle especially more lethal at close range than the standard model. The Corean Enterprises MacAdams-Suharno facility on Stewart performed these conversions during the Late Succession Wars. The heavier autocannon allows a single crew to threaten targets that would otherwise require multiple standard Vedettes to engage effectively. The conversion was limited by spare fusion engine availability and remained uncommon outside Free Worlds League forces. It is best used in close terrain where the AC/10's shorter optimal range is less limiting and per-shot damage is most valuable.

The AC/2 variant emerged in 2963 as a field modification to extend the Vedette's effective engagement range, replacing the AC/5 with a lighter autocannon and adding an SRM-2 for close defense. The configuration is suited to patrol and screening duties where long-range harassment is preferred over direct engagement. Crews can maintain harassing fire at ranges that discourage return fire from most other vehicle types, while the SRM-2 provides short-range punch against exposed targets. The straightforward nature of the modification allows field application with minimal specialized tooling, making it a common improvisation in any unit operating standard Vedettes for extended periods without depot resupply.

text.deployment: The Armor Vedette of the ilClan era represents the accumulated results of more than a century of incremental improvement applied to the original hull. Built on the fuel cell platform pioneered by the Cell variant, it mounts an Ultra AC/10, heavy machine gun, and heavy ferro-fibrous armor in the heaviest configuration ever applied to the standard Vedette hull. The moniker 'Armor Vedette' distinguishes it as a qualitatively different vehicle from earlier variants despite the shared lineage. Multiple manufacturers across competing factions produce it simultaneously, making parts widely available. CASE protects the ammunition bins. The vehicle is best employed in line-breaking and direct fire support roles, delivering heavy autocannon fire while absorbing punishment that would destroy earlier variants.

Developed exclusively for sale to the Trinity Alliance, the LB-X variant trades the Ultra autocannon for an LB 5-X that provides organic anti-aircraft capability through its cluster munition option. The restoration of the machine gun improves anti-infantry defense that the Ultra variant had sacrificed. This variant is rare outside Capellan-influenced space and the Magistracy of Canopus, where it serves in combined arms formations that need a medium vehicle capable of contributing to aerospace denial. Against ground targets, standard LB rounds maintain effectiveness against light and medium armor.

The 2968 Liao variant is a Capellan response to energy weapon availability and ammunition shortage during the Succession Wars. Replacing the autocannon with twin medium lasers and a power amplifier eliminates dependence on autocannon rounds, a significant advantage during extended campaigns in areas where resupply is unreliable. Capellan logisticians found the trade worthwhile, and the variant remains common in Capellan space for operations where ammunition supply chains are stretched. The medium laser loadout performs well against lightly armored targets, though effective range is shorter than the standard model. Units deploying this variant tend to close to engagement ranges below standard doctrine to compensate.

The Light Gauss variant is NETC's range-extension approach, replacing all armament with a single Light Gauss Rifle to engage targets at distances that keep the vehicle safely outside most opponents' effective return fire envelope. The trade comes at the cost of reduced close-range capability and somewhat lighter ferro-fibrous armor. The variant is best suited to deep screening and delaying operations, where accurate long-range fire and rapid repositioning matter more than sustained firepower. Its ammunition dependence requires attentive logistics, and crews need fire discipline to avoid wasting ammunition on targets better handled by other elements in the formation.

New Earth Trading Company's own advanced upgrade retains the machine gun and uses a ferro-fibrous armor package slightly more modest than Hellespont's competing Ultra variant, positioning it as a more economical modernization path. The Ultra AC/5 provides enhanced rate of fire while NETC's ComStar-sourced electronics maintain the reliability advantage of the original. The variant is most common in Lyran and Federated Suns forces operating within NETC's distribution network. Produced from 3056 onward, it slots easily into existing Vedette logistics chains and requires no special maintenance procedures beyond those already established in any formation already operating standard Vedettes.

The Rotary AC/5 variant is NETC's premium offering, providing maximum sustained firepower from the Vedette hull. The rotary autocannon's fire rate significantly exceeds any other weapon option available on the platform, allowing a single vehicle to suppress targets that would require multiple standard Vedettes working together. Introduced in 3067 as a direct Hellespont competitor, it targets buyers who prioritize damage output over unit cost. The variant demands attentive crew discipline regarding heat management and ammunition consumption, but in practiced hands it excels as an ambush platform. It appears in both House and mercenary formations able to support the higher per-vehicle price and associated logistics requirements.

The Ultra variant is Hellespont Industrials' first modernization of the Vedette, introduced in 3054 for buyers who could afford a modest technology premium. The Imperator Ultra series autocannon's enhanced fire rate effectively doubles peak damage output, and replacement of standard plate with Hellespont Lite ferro-fibrous armor improves survivability by roughly 20 percent. The variant appeals to units seeking a direct upgrade path from the standard model without extensive crew retraining or logistical disruption. Hellespont markets it to Capellan commands and Trinity Alliance forces, and it sees use in both front-line and second-echelon armored formations that require improved firepower without a fundamental change in vehicle doctrine.

The V-G7X is an experimental prototype created at Field Center ARCT Gemini 7 on Arcturus during the Jihad period, exploring the limits of what the Vedette hull could theoretically achieve. The supercharged XL engine pushes the vehicle to 108 km/h, a speed practical for fast scouting and exploitation operations rather than standard line engagements. Dual independent turrets allow the Bombast Laser and Light Autocannon/5 to engage separate targets simultaneously, a capability unavailable on any standard variant. Reactive armor provides protection against ballistic and missile threats most likely encountered at the speeds this vehicle operates. Only a few dozen were built before the prohibitive price deterred procurement. Its conceptual influence is visible in the later V7 and V9 variants that simplified its ideas into practical production configurations.

The V7 is Arcturan Arms' production answer to market criticism that drove buyers away from the expensive V-G7X prototype. Replacing the supercharged XL engine with a fuel cell and stripping the targeting computer and secondary turret, Arcturan retained only the Bombast Laser and paired Magshot Gauss Rifles in a much more affordable package. Heavy ferro-fibrous armor and CASE provide crew survivability even in sustained engagements. The result is a bare-bones vehicle cheaper than its predecessor but retaining the ammo-independent primary weapon valued by mercenaries and militia forces with constrained logistics. Introduced in 3084 and noted for its design quirks, it has sold steadily to Lyran Commonwealth and mercenary customers as a reliable fuel cell alternative to the standard ICE Vedette.

The V9 represents Arcturan Arms' Dark Age evolution of the fuel cell Vedette concept, introduced in 3105 for Lyran and later Clan Wolf customers on Arcturus. Retaining the fuel cell engine from the V7 lineage, it mounts a standard Gauss rifle as its primary anti-armor weapon, providing long-range precision that pairs effectively with the chassis's mobility. Paired Magshot Gauss Rifles address infantry and light armor threats. Reflective armor provides crew protection specifically suited to operations against energy-weapon-equipped opponents, a common threat in the Dark Age environment. The V9 fills a niche role requiring specific tactical contexts to fully exploit, but within those roles it delivers considerable lethality at ranges that keep it safe from most direct counterfire.

Exclusive to the SLDF Royal Divisions, this 2761 upgrade represented the pinnacle of Von Luckner capability during the Star League era. An extralight fusion engine freed sufficient tonnage for dual LB 10-X Autocannons, four Streak SRM-2 launchers, a Small Pulse Laser, and an Artemis IV FCS enhancing the LRM rack. Issued only to Royal Division armored formations, Royal Von Luckners survived the Amaris Civil War primarily in the hands of units that departed with General Kerensky on the Exodus, making surviving examples in the Inner Sphere extraordinarily rare. The Word of Blake later drew on this variant's design principles when developing the VNL-K65W.

The Star League-era production standard, this variant served as the baseline Von Luckner for SLDF combined-arms formations throughout the height of the Star League. Deployed alongside BattleMechs in defensive lances, it covered supply lines and fortified positions on both Hegemony core worlds and Periphery garrison stations. The upgrade introduced ferro-fibrous armor protection on the vehicle's flanks, a Streak SRM missile complement, and improved LRM capability with Artemis IV fire control, giving SLDF crews better accuracy without the logistical burden of the base model's standard launchers. Production at both Bryant and Pardeau supplied the SLDF and, eventually, member state auxiliaries.

Developed by the Federated Suns around 3002 as an experimental close-combat upgrade, the K100 strips the entire missile complement from the standard configuration to mount a second Armstrong Autocannon/20 in the turret. The result is a vehicle of terrifying short-range lethality, capable of delivering an overwhelming volume of autocannon fire against any target within range. The Federated Suns deployed the K100 for urban assault and fortified strong-points where twin autocannons could dominate confined approaches, trading the original's versatility for concentrated punch and simplified ammunition logistics.

The primary production configuration of the Von Luckner from its 2612 introduction through the decline of the Succession Wars, the K65N was the most widely distributed variant. HartfordCo supplied it to SLDF forces from both the Bryant and Pardeau facilities, with the latter expanding during the late Star League period to meet growing demand. After Bryant's destruction in 2840 ended production, surviving K65Ns were pressed into increasingly prolonged service across the Great House militaries. By 3039, concentrated primarily in the forces of Houses Davion, Steiner, Kurita, and Marik, the remaining examples were jealously maintained as assets whose replacement was simply not possible.

The Draconis Combine's 3008 refit of the Von Luckner prioritizes sustained combat over raw short-range shock. The Armstrong Autocannon/20 is downgraded to a SarLon MaxiCannon AC/10, while a HellStar PPC is added to the turret alongside it. The twin Holly SRM-6 launchers are removed to accommodate the PPC's bulk and heat output. The result is a tank far less dependent on expendable ammunition, capable of sustained long-range engagement, and well-suited to DCMS formations operating far from established supply bases. The K70 saw steady Combine service through the Succession Wars and into the Clan Invasion era.

Introduced during the FedCom Civil War as a DCMS modernization, the K75N significantly upgrades the Von Luckner's offensive capability. An Ultra AC/20 and SRM-6 launcher occupy the turret alongside a pair of medium lasers, while a forward-firing MRM-20 and twin machine guns provide hull-mounted support. The K75N served as the conceptual template for the later K85N development program at Sapphire Metals, and saw active DCMS service during the Civil War and Jihad periods. Although never a strict factory-line production vehicle, the K75N demonstrated that the Von Luckner airframe could accommodate modern DCMS weaponry and laid the groundwork for the Shimonita production revival.

Sapphire Metals' flagship Von Luckner for the Draconis Combine, the K85N combines an XL engine and hardened armor with a weapon suite optimized for close-quarters urban fighting. An LB 20-X Autocannon provides the primary punch, supported by twin Holly SRM-6 launchers and a Shigunga MRM-10 for sustained close-range fire. A Firestorm Flamer and SperryBrowning Machine Gun retain the classic anti-infantry capability. Designed for the tight confines of city streets, it has proven decisive across multiple DCMS campaigns and has become the standard Von Luckner configuration in active Combine service. The K85N is produced at the Sapphire Metals facility on Shimonita, which previously performed K75N-standard refits before DCMS reoccupation.

Developed in parallel with the K85N at Sapphire Metals, the K90 takes the same hardened armor and XL engine in a longer-range direction. A Gauss rifle replaces the autocannon as the primary weapon, supported by a Snub-nose PPC and a reduced single SRM-4 launcher. Intended as an MBT-style offensive vehicle capable of engaging at ranges that would neutralize the K85N's close-quarters advantage, the K90 saw limited testing during the Battle of New Avalon in 3146. The DCMS has not committed to full production, leaving the K90 primarily in evaluation and special-issue service.

This experimental refit, adapted from captured or clandestinely obtained VNL-K70 hulls, first appeared in Republic space around 3076 in the hands of yakuza syndicates operating across Prefectures I through III. An LB 20-X Autocannon, Medium Pulse Laser, and SRM-4 with Artemis IV FCS fill the turret, while approximately thirty tons of hardened armor make the vehicle exceptionally difficult to destroy. A modified communications system reportedly defeats most electronic countermeasures. The variant was observed deployed against Blakist forces during the Jihad as well as against Republic security services. Whether produced at a hidden facility or supplied covertly by the Draconis Combine remains unconfirmed, and the VNL-X71 carries Design Quirks reflecting its Improved Communications and unconventional maintenance requirements.

The H-10 was a radical departure from the Warrior's attack heritage, replacing most offensive systems with a five-ton infantry bay designed to carry a complete battle armor point. Intended as a high-speed airmobile transport, the H-10 gives infantry commanders the ability to deploy battle armor rapidly across terrain that ground vehicles cannot navigate efficiently. Its pair of machine guns provides minimal self-defense capability. The design has been adopted primarily by Lyran Commonwealth forces and a smaller number of mercenary commands willing to invest in dedicated airmobile infantry tactics.

The H-7 spread beyond the Lyran Commonwealth within years of its introduction, finding operators in every Successor State and across the Periphery. House Davion's Ceti Hussars and the Free Worlds Guards maintained substantial numbers, as did the Capellan Home Guard. Smaller mercenary outfits built entire air cavalry companies around the design. During the Fourth Succession War, Warriors supporting Davion airmobile operations demonstrated the design's effectiveness across varied terrain types. Despite its age, the H-7 continued to see service well into the Jihad period wherever maintenance pipelines remained intact.

The H-7A addressed the SarLon AC/2's firepower limitations by pairing a machine gun with an upgraded SarLon Maxicannon 5, sacrificing the SRM launcher for increased close-range output. The variant was adopted primarily by mercenary commands and operators who preferred the heavier autocannon profile for anti-helicopter and anti-infantry engagements. It saw less adoption among state militaries, which tended to favor the H-7C's standoff capability for fire support missions.

The H-7C replaced the SarLon autocannon system entirely with a long-range missile battery, reconfiguring the Warrior as a standoff bombardment platform. It found favor with commanders who wanted indirect fire support from a fast, low-signature vehicle rather than a static artillery asset. State militaries and Periphery forces operating in open terrain adopted the variant for its ability to engage targets at distances where return fire from conventional weapons was less effective.

The H-8 became the standard Warrior variant across the Lyran Commonwealth military and spread rapidly to the Federated Suns, Free Rasalhague Republic, and a host of Periphery states and mercenary commands. Its fusion engine reduced logistical complexity compared to ICE-powered predecessors, and the missile armament gave it genuine punch against armored targets at range. After the FedCom Civil War, the AFFS, FRR, and Periphery nations placed orders that forced Lockheed/CBM to build additional production lines to meet demand. The H-8 remains the most widely produced Warrior variant.

The H-9 replaced the H-8's missile suite with a Thor Rotary 40mm autocannon, offering sustained direct fire capability in a single weapon system. The variant trades the H-8's range flexibility for raw firepower in close engagements, making it a preferred choice for commanders operating in urban terrain or environments where sustained missile ammunition supply is uncertain. It has seen adoption across most of the same operators as the H-8, typically supplementing rather than replacing the base variant within the same formations.
